material_units.source_text:
Definition — Occupancy measure
      
        For a policy $\pi$ and initial law $\mu$, the (normalised, discounted) occupancy measure is
        $$\rho_\pi(s,a) := (1-\gamma)\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^t\,\mathbb P^{\pi}_{\mu}(s_t=s,\ a_t=a),\qquad \rho_\pi(s):=\sum_a\rho_\pi(s,a).$$
        It is a probability measure on $\mathcal S\times\mathcal A$ (the weights $(1-\gamma)\gamma^t$ sum to one), and every discounted return is an expectation under it:
        $$J_r(\pi)=\frac{1}{1-\gamma}\sum_{s,a}\rho_\pi(s,a)\,r(s,a)=\frac{\langle\rho_\pi,r\rangle}{1-\gamma},\qquad J_{c_i}(\pi)=\frac{\langle\rho_\pi,c_i\rangle}{1-\gamma}.$$
        Altman writes $f_\alpha(\beta,u;x,a)=(1-\alpha)\sum_{t\ge1}\alpha^{t-1}P^u_\beta(X_t=x,A_t=a)$ for the same object (time starts at 1 there).
